phrases.translation: They will be humble with the believers but firm towards the disbelievers, struggling in the Way of Allah;
phrases.explanation: The promised people combine humility and mercy toward believers with firmness toward disbelievers and striving in Allah’s way. Humility prevents arrogance within the community, while firmness prevents surrender to hostility. Their struggle remains within what Allah commands and permits, so firmness cannot be used to cancel the justice and restraint required elsewhere.

phrases.translation: fearing no blame from anyone.
phrases.explanation: They do not fear anyone’s blame when obeying Allah. Criticism, ridicule, and social pressure cannot move them from a known duty. This courage complements their humility: they are gentle with fellow believers without becoming dependent on public approval, and firm without needing to display toughness for its own sake.

phrases.translation: This is the favour of Allah.
phrases.explanation: The qualities and replacement community just described are Allah’s favour, not an achievement generated by ethnic pride or self-congratulation. Faith, love, courage, and steadfastness are gifts for which gratitude is due. The wording keeps hope open to those whom Allah chooses rather than making one group permanently superior by name.

phrases.translation: He grants it to whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Allah grants this favour to whom He wills. No one can claim it automatically through ancestry, slogans, or affiliation. The promise assures believers that sincere replacements will arise, but the bestowal remains divine. Human beings must respond with faith and character rather than assuming the description already applies to them.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: Allah’s bounty is vast, and His knowledge encompasses those who truly love and serve Him. His generosity means that the loss of apostates does not exhaust His resources, while His knowledge ensures that sincere faith is distinguished from performance. The two names fittingly close a promise about divine favour and hidden loyalty.

phrases.translation: Your only guardians are Allah, His Messenger, and fellow believers—who establish prayer and pay alms-tax with humility
phrases.explanation: True protective loyalty belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and believers characterized by prayer, almsgiving, and humility. This answers the search for security through opposing alliances by identifying the believing relationship that actually sustains the community. Religious loyalty is not based on words alone, since worship, generosity, and submission mark the believers described.

phrases.translation: Whoever allies themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and fellow believers, then it is certainly Allah’s party that will prevail
phrases.explanation: Those who ally themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers belong to Allah’s party, which will ultimately prevail. The promise answers fear of changing fortunes with confidence in divine support. Prevailing is not a guarantee of effortless success in every immediate event, but assurance that final victory does not belong to betrayal and opportunism.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not seek the guardianship of those given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers who have made your faith a mockery and amusement.
phrases.explanation: The prohibition is qualified by conduct: it concerns those from earlier scriptural communities and the disbelievers who make the believers’ religion a mockery and amusement. Such mockers are not to be trusted as protective allies against the faith. The wording does not condemn peaceful relations with every person who received an earlier scripture, since the target is expressly those who ridicule it.

phrases.translation: And be mindful of Allah if you are ˹truly˺ believers
phrases.explanation: Mindfulness of Allah is presented as a condition of genuine faith when choosing alliances. Believers must consider whether a professed source of protection actually opposes their religion and mocks its practices. Reverence requires avoiding that contradictory dependence while continuing to distinguish hostile conduct from the identity of every outsider.

phrases.translation: When you call to prayer, they mock it in amusement.
phrases.explanation: The mockery becomes concrete when the call to prayer is treated as entertainment. This is not ordinary disagreement about belief but ridicule of an act of worship intended to gather believers before Allah. The example shows why such people cannot simultaneously serve as guardians of the religious community they deride.

phrases.translation: This is because they are a people without understanding
phrases.explanation: Their lack of understanding concerns failure to grasp the purpose of prayer and the consequences of mocking it, not a statement about innate intelligence or ethnicity. Commentary explains that they do not appreciate the benefit of responding to the call or the seriousness of deriding it. Spiritual heedlessness produces the disrespect described.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Do you resent us only because we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before—while most of you are rebellious?”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet asks whether the mockers resent the believers merely for faith in Allah, the Quran, and earlier revelations. The question exposes the irrationality of ridiculing beliefs that affirm revelation shared with earlier communities. Its closing criticism of rebellion belongs to the people being addressed in this dispute and should not be detached as a description of every Jew or Christian.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of those who deserve a worse punishment from Allah ˹than the rebellious˺?
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to ask whether he should identify a punishment worse than the conduct for which the believers are being resented. The rhetorical question reverses the mockers’ assumed moral superiority. It directs attention from ridiculing Muslim worship to Allah’s own judgment of serious rebellion.

phrases.translation: It is those who earned Allah’s condemnation and displeasure—some being reduced to apes and pigs and worshippers of false gods.
phrases.explanation: Those described earned Allah’s condemnation and anger, with some transformed into apes and pigs and others associated with worshipping false powers. The verse reports judgment on particular transgressors in sacred history. It must not be converted into an ethnic description of later Jews or Christians, since the basis stated is divine condemnation for conduct, not ancestry.

phrases.translation: These are far worse in rank and farther astray from the Right Way.”
phrases.explanation: Their rank is worse and their path farther astray according to Allah’s judgment. The comparison concerns moral and spiritual standing after persistent rebellion, not permission for human beings to degrade entire populations. It concludes the response to mockery by locating true dishonour in alienation from Allah rather than in being ridiculed by people.

phrases.translation: When they come to you ˹believers˺ they say, “We believe.”
phrases.explanation: The hypocrites addressed in this passage announce faith when they meet the believers. Their declaration is an outward performance intended to secure acceptance, not a sincere change of conviction. The immediate description concerns a specific deceptive group, not every visitor or every member of the wider religious community from which they came.

phrases.translation: But they are committed to disbelief when they enter and when they leave.
phrases.explanation: They enter and leave with the same concealed disbelief, showing that the encounter never touched their inward commitment. Their words did not represent hesitation that developed into faith or faith that later failed. The duplicity remained constant from arrival to departure, hidden from human listeners but fully present in their own hearts.

phrases.translation: And Allah knows what they hide
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what they conceal, so private disbelief cannot be made harmless by public professions of faith. This knowledge also means that final judgment does not depend on whether the believers successfully expose every hypocrite. Human beings may hear only words, but Allah knows the conviction and intention behind them.

phrases.translation: You see many of them racing towards sin, transgression, and consumption of forbidden gain.
phrases.explanation: Many of the people under discussion hasten into sin, aggression, and forbidden gain. The wording says many rather than all, keeping the accusation tied to observable conduct within the group addressed. Their eagerness shows habitual commitment to wrongdoing, including unlawful earnings such as the corrupt payments associated with distorted judgment in the surrounding passage.

phrases.translation: Evil indeed are their actions
phrases.explanation: Their actions are condemned as evil because they combine disobedience, violation of others’ rights, and consumption of unlawful wealth. The moral judgment is not based on communal identity but on what they repeatedly do. This short verdict prepares for the next question about leaders who fail to oppose such conduct.

phrases.translation: Why do their rabbis and scholars not forbid them from saying what is sinful and consuming what is unlawful?
phrases.explanation: Rabbis and scholars are questioned for not forbidding sinful speech and unlawful consumption. Their knowledge and leadership create responsibility to correct wrongdoing rather than watch silently or benefit from it. In this setting, corrupt speech includes lies about Allah and His rulings, while unlawful gain includes bribes connected with judgment.

phrases.translation: Evil indeed is their inaction
phrases.explanation: The leaders’ inaction is itself condemned as evil. Failing to restrain known wrong is not neutral when one possesses religious authority and the ability to speak. Silence can allow sin and exploitation to appear accepted. The verse therefore places moral responsibility on teachers and leaders as well as on the immediate offenders.

phrases.translation: ˹Some among˺ the Jews said, “Allah is tight-fisted.”
phrases.explanation: The quoted claim that Allah is tight-fisted attributes stinginess or restricted power to Him. It insults the Giver rather than merely expressing human poverty or disappointment. The translation’s qualification, some among the Jews, is important: the statement is attributed to particular speakers and is not a claim that every Jewish person said or believed it.

phrases.translation: May their fists be tied and they be condemned for what they said.
phrases.explanation: The response ties their own hands and condemns them for what they said, turning their accusation back upon them in divine requital. Their speech has moral consequences because it misrepresents Allah with insolence. The report of this judgment does not authorize later readers to repeat the statement as a slogan against an entire community.

phrases.translation: Rather, He is open-handed, giving freely as He pleases.
phrases.explanation: Allah’s open-handedness is affirmed against the accusation of stinginess. He gives and spends according to His will, without exhaustion or dependence on human permission. The image emphasizes unrestricted generosity and power. It assures the believers that an opponent’s insult cannot diminish Allah’s ability to provide or fulfil His purpose.

phrases.translation: That which has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ from your Lord will only cause many of them to increase in wickedness and disbelief.
phrases.explanation: Further revelation increases many of the addressed opponents in transgression and disbelief because they respond to clearer truth with greater obstinacy. The revelation is not defective or a cause of evil in itself. Their rejection hardens in reaction to it, exposing a deliberate refusal to submit even when hidden matters are made clear.

phrases.translation: We have stirred among them hostility and hatred until the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: Hostility and hatred are said to be cast among them until Judgment Day. Al-Tabari understood the parties here as Jews and Christians, in contrast with the intra-Christian reading he preferred for a similar statement earlier. The verse describes a consequence of rebellion and division, not an instruction for others to promote hostility.

phrases.translation: Whenever they kindle the fire of war, Allah puts it out.
phrases.explanation: Whenever they kindle war, Allah extinguishes it. The fire image presents war as something deliberately ignited through planning and hostility, while its extinction shows divine power to frustrate those designs. Human military preparation cannot secure success against His will, and apparent momentum toward conflict does not place events beyond His control.

phrases.translation: And they strive to spread corruption in the land.
phrases.explanation: They are further described as actively striving to spread corruption in the land. Corruption here includes persistent disobedience, denial of Allah’s signs and messengers, and conduct that damages right order. The wording emphasizes sustained effort rather than an isolated mistake, explaining the severity of the surrounding condemnation.

phrases.translation: And Allah does not like corruptors
phrases.explanation: Allah does not love those who spread corruption. This concise judgment defines the moral issue behind the war, dishonesty, and transgression just described. Religious heritage or claims to revelation cannot make corrupt conduct beloved to Him. The statement measures people by their actions and their opposition to His guidance.

phrases.translation: Had the People of the Book only been faithful and mindful ˹of Allah˺, We would have certainly absolved them of their sins and admitted them into the Gardens of Bliss
phrases.explanation: A direct promise of forgiveness and gardens of bliss is offered to the People of the Book if they believe and remain mindful of Allah. Al-Tabari explains the required faith as including affirmation of Muhammad and obedience to Allah’s prohibitions. The verse prevents collective despair or condemnation by holding open sincere faith, reform, forgiveness, and Paradise.

phrases.translation: And had they observed the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have been overwhelmed with provisions from above and below.
phrases.explanation: Observing the Torah, Gospel, and further revelation from their Lord would bring abundant provision from above and below. Al-Tabari includes the guidance brought by Muhammad within what was sent to them. The imagery suggests blessings such as rain and earth’s produce. Their fundamental loss is tied to failing to practise revelation rather than lacking access to it.

phrases.translation: Some among them are upright, yet many do nothing but evil
phrases.explanation: The verse explicitly recognizes an upright group among the People of the Book while condemning the evil deeds of many others. This distinction prevents a sweeping judgment against every individual. Al-Tabari described uprightness as a moderate, truthful position concerning Jesus, neither deifying him nor insulting him. Conduct and belief remain the basis of evaluation.

phrases.translation: O Messenger! Convey everything revealed to you from your Lord.
phrases.explanation: The Messenger must convey everything revealed by his Lord, including unwelcome criticism and commands that provoke opposition. He may not soften the mission by withholding difficult portions. Complete delivery is a trust, and the surrounding interfaith disputes make clear why courage is needed to announce truth without tailoring it to the audience’s preferences.

phrases.translation: If you do not, then you have not delivered His message.
phrases.explanation: Failing to convey the revelation would amount to failing to deliver Allah’s message. Commentary stresses that withholding even part of an entrusted communication can betray the mission as a whole. The Prophet’s responsibility is therefore not measured by popularity or by how much listeners accept, but by faithful transmission of what he received.

phrases.translation: Allah will ˹certainly˺ protect you from the people.
phrases.explanation: Allah promises to protect the Messenger from the people, removing fear as a reason for silence. Reports proposed different occasions for this assurance, including threats against his life. Its function in the verse is clear: the Messenger can proclaim the full message despite hostile numbers or plots because their power does not exceed Allah’s protection.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah does not guide the people who disbelieve
phrases.explanation: Allah does not guide those who persist in disbelief, so the Messenger’s successful delivery cannot be measured by whether every opponent believes. His task is proclamation, while guidance remains Allah’s work. The statement reinforces the command not to let resistant audiences determine which parts of the message may be spoken.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! You have nothing to stand on unless you observe the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord.”
phrases.explanation: The People of the Book are told that they have no firm religious standing unless they uphold the Torah, Gospel, and what Allah has revealed to them. Al-Tabari includes Muhammad’s message in that further revelation. The demand is for consistent practice and acceptance of Allah’s messengers, not selective honour for one scripture while rejecting another.

phrases.translation: And your Lord’s revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ will only cause many of them to increase in wickedness and disbelief.
phrases.explanation: Many of the opponents respond to the Prophet’s revelation with increased transgression and disbelief. Their greater rejection follows greater clarification, not a lack of evidence. The statement repeats that hostile response to truth can deepen culpability. It prepares the Messenger for resistance without permitting him to dilute the revelation.

phrases.translation: So do not grieve for the people who disbelieve
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told not to grieve over people who choose disbelief after the message has been conveyed. This does not forbid compassion or continued invitation. It frees him from crushing sorrow over decisions he cannot control and redirects him to his own responsibility of faithful delivery and obedience.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the believers, Jews, Sabians and Christians—whoever ˹truly˺ believes in Allah and the Last Day and does good, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: Believers, Jews, Sabians, and Christians are named, but the promise is conditioned on genuine faith in Allah and the Last Day together with righteous deeds. Communal labels alone do not secure the outcome. Whoever meets those conditions is promised freedom from ultimate fear and grief, offering hope across communal boundaries while retaining clear moral and spiritual requirements.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent them messengers.
phrases.explanation: Allah recalls both His covenant with the Children of Israel and the messengers sent to guide them. These were repeated favours that made the required response clear. The covenant concerned worship and obedience, while successive messengers brought warning and good news. The history therefore begins with generous guidance rather than neglect.

phrases.translation: Whenever a messenger came to them with what they did not desire, they denied some and killed others
phrases.explanation: When messengers brought teachings that conflicted with desire, the offenders denied some and killed others. Their criterion was appetite rather than truth, escalating from rejection of speech to violence against Allah’s emissaries. The statement describes a recurrent pattern among those being judged in this history, not a claim that every Israelite participated in killing a prophet.

phrases.translation: They thought there would be no consequences, so they turned a blind eye and a deaf ear.
phrases.explanation: The offenders assumed that no trial or punishment would follow their treatment of the messengers, so they became metaphorically blind and deaf to guidance. Their senses were not necessarily impaired. They chose not to see or hear what challenged them. False security about consequences made continued rejection feel safe.

phrases.translation: Yet Allah turned to them in forgiveness ˹after their repentance˺, but again many became blind and deaf.
phrases.explanation: Allah accepted their return in forgiveness after repentance, yet many later became blind and deaf again. The verse records both real divine mercy and recurring human relapse. It also says many rather than all, distinguishing those who returned to rejection from others. Earlier forgiveness did not make later deliberate heedlessness impossible.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do
phrases.explanation: Allah sees everything they do, including the conduct hidden behind assumed immunity and outward religious identity. No act of denial, violence, repentance, or relapse escapes Him. His perfect seeing undermines the assumption that unobserved wrongdoing carries no consequence and assures that every response is known accurately.

phrases.translation: Those who say, “Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary,” have certainly fallen into disbelief.
phrases.explanation: Identifying Allah with the Messiah, son of Mary, is rejected as disbelief. The verse addresses this doctrinal claim directly while the following words honour Jesus as a teacher of monotheism. Rejecting his deification is therefore not denying his prophetic status or permission to insult those who revere him.

phrases.translation: The Messiah ˹himself˺ said, “O Children of Israel! Worship Allah—my Lord and your Lord.”
phrases.explanation: Jesus himself calls the Children of Israel to worship Allah, whom he describes as my Lord and your Lord. His own words distinguish the worshipper from the Lord he worships and place him alongside his people in servitude. This provides the strongest response to the claim that he is Allah.

phrases.translation: Whoever associates others with Allah ˹in worship˺ will surely be forbidden Paradise by Allah.
phrases.explanation: Associating partners with Allah in worship results in being forbidden Paradise. The warning is general and concerns giving created beings the worship due to Allah alone. It follows Jesus’ command to worship his Lord, making clear that honouring a messenger cannot justify turning that messenger into another object of divinity.

phrases.translation: Their home will be the Fire.
phrases.explanation: The Fire is named as the home of those who persist in this association. The warning states the consequence plainly rather than treating false worship as a harmless difference of terminology. It must be read with the next verses’ invitation to repent, which leaves a way back before final judgment.

phrases.translation: And the wrongdoers will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: Wrongdoers will have no helpers able to rescue them from Allah’s judgment. No religious figure, community, or patron can overturn the consequence of persistent association with Him. The absence of helpers concerns ultimate deliverance from divine punishment, not the ordinary assistance people may legitimately offer one another in worldly life.

phrases.translation: Those who say, “Allah is one in a Trinity,” have certainly fallen into disbelief.
phrases.explanation: Saying that Allah is one in a Trinity, expressed in commentary as the third of three, is also rejected as disbelief. The verse follows the identification of Jesus with Allah and addresses the resulting doctrine of divinity. Its criticism is directed at the claim about Allah, not at a license for contempt toward Christian people.

phrases.translation: There is only One God.
phrases.explanation: The correction is concise: there is only One God. Divine worship and ultimate lordship cannot be distributed among Jesus, Mary, or any other created being. This statement supplies the positive monotheistic foundation after rejecting the preceding formulation, returning attention to the same truth Jesus himself taught.

phrases.translation: If they do not stop saying this, those who disbelieve among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: A painful punishment is threatened if they do not stop making this claim. The condition matters because it calls for abandonment of the false statement rather than presenting punishment as unavoidable regardless of response. Those who disbelieve are warned, while the next verse immediately invites them toward repentance and forgiveness.

phrases.translation: Will they not turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness?
phrases.explanation: The rhetorical question invites those holding the two rejected doctrines to turn back to Allah and seek His forgiveness. Even serious false speech about Him is not placed beyond repentance while the opportunity remains. The verse asks for a change of direction and an explicit request for pardon rather than despair or defensive persistence.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah’s forgiveness and mercy make the invitation to repent meaningful. He accepts the return of those who abandon disobedience and seek pardon. The warning about punishment is therefore not the only message given to the doctrinal offenders. Mercy is openly available to sincere repentance, including after grave error about Allah.

phrases.translation: The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger.
phrases.explanation: The Messiah is described as a messenger, affirming a genuine and honoured prophetic role while rejecting divinity. Calling him no more than a messenger does not make him insignificant. It places him within the highest human mission of conveying Allah’s guidance, without confusing that mission with being the Lord who sent him.

phrases.translation: ˹Many˺ messengers had ˹come and˺ gone before him.
phrases.explanation: Messengers came and passed before Jesus, locating him within a succession of servants sent at particular times. He is not an eternal exception whose existence stands outside created prophetic history. The continuity of messengers also reinforces that the proper response to him is to receive Allah’s message rather than worship the messenger.

phrases.translation: His mother was a woman of truth.
phrases.explanation: Mary is honoured as a woman of truth. This affirms her exceptional sincerity and piety while retaining her human status. It answers both slander against her and any attempt to turn her into a goddess. The verse can therefore honour mother and son deeply without assigning divine attributes to either.

phrases.translation: They both ate food.
phrases.explanation: Jesus and Mary both ate food, an ordinary sign of bodily need and created human life. Dependence on nourishment distinguishes them from Allah, who is not sustained by His creatures. The argument does not deny Jesus’ miracles or spiritual rank. It uses a shared human fact to challenge the inference that such rank equals divinity.

phrases.translation: See how We make the signs clear to them, yet see how they are deluded ˹from the truth˺
phrases.explanation: Allah makes the signs clear, yet people can still be turned away from their implications. The problem is not ambiguity in the evidence about Jesus’ humanity and messengership. It is the response of those who continue in error after clarification. The repeated call to see invites reflection on both the proof and the puzzling refusal of it.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “How can you worship besides Allah those who can neither harm nor benefit you?
phrases.explanation: The Prophet challenges worship of beings that possess no independent power to harm or benefit. Applied to Jesus and other revered figures, the argument concerns ultimate divine control, not whether Allah may perform miracles or grant benefit through His servants. Whatever creatures do occurs only within His permission, so worship belongs to Him alone.

phrases.translation: And Allah ˹alone˺ is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”
phrases.explanation: Allah alone is All-Hearing and All-Knowing, unlike objects of worship that cannot independently answer or govern. He hears those who call upon Him and knows their needs, claims, and intentions. These attributes make Him the proper recipient of worship and expose the futility of directing ultimate reliance toward powerless creatures.

phrases.translation: Say, “O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes in your faith beyond the truth, nor follow the vain desires of those who went astray before ˹you˺.
phrases.explanation: The People of the Book must not exaggerate in religion beyond truth or inherit the desires of earlier people who strayed. In context, exaggeration includes deifying Jesus, while al-Tabari also contrasts the opposite error of slandering him and Mary. Faithful speech must remain within revealed truth, avoiding both excessive exaltation and unjust denigration.

phrases.translation: They misled many and strayed from the Right Way.”
phrases.explanation: Earlier strayers misled many others while themselves departing from the right way. Their influence and popularity did not prove their guidance. The warning discourages inherited religious error: a teaching should not be accepted merely because predecessors, scholars, or large communities repeated it when it conflicts with Allah’s truth.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers among the Children of Israel were condemned in the revelations of David and Jesus, son of Mary.
phrases.explanation: Disbelievers among the Children of Israel were condemned through David and Jesus. The wording restricts the condemnation to the disbelievers rather than every descendant. It also shows that rejection of truth was opposed within their own prophetic tradition, not invented as a later external criticism of their community.

phrases.translation: That was for their disobedience and violations
phrases.explanation: The stated reasons for condemnation are disobedience and repeated transgression of Allah’s limits. The basis is conduct and response to revelation, not ancestry. This explicit explanation prevents the previous reference from being read as an inherited curse and keeps attention on the actions that earned prophetic condemnation.

phrases.translation: They did not forbid one another from doing evil.
phrases.explanation: They failed to forbid one another from committing evil. This communal silence allowed wrongdoing to continue without correction and made the wider group complicit in its normalization. The verse follows earlier criticism of scholars who did not restrain sinful speech and unlawful gain, reinforcing responsibility to oppose known wrong within one’s own community.

phrases.translation: Evil indeed was what they did
phrases.explanation: Their conduct is condemned as evil, including both the wrongdoing itself and the failure to restrain it. A community cannot preserve moral standing merely by avoiding every act personally while approving or ignoring the same acts among its members. The verdict ties individual sin to collective negligence.

phrases.translation: You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies.
phrases.explanation: Many of those criticized take disbelievers as protective allies while opposing Allah’s messengers and friends. Commentary identifies alliances with idolaters in the historical setting. As in the earlier guardianship passage, the issue is allegiance joined to hostility toward faith, not ordinary kindness, trade, or peaceful contact with every disbeliever.

phrases.translation: Truly wicked are their misdeeds, which have earned them Allah’s wrath.
phrases.explanation: Their own deeds have gone ahead of them and earned Allah’s anger. The image of sending deeds forward emphasizes personal responsibility: future judgment meets what people themselves have done. Their alliances and hostility are not blamed on fate or ancestry, and their anger-producing record cannot be disowned when they return to Allah.

phrases.translation: And they will be in everlasting torment
phrases.explanation: Everlasting torment concludes the warning for those whose record ends in this rebellion. The severity reflects persistent disbelief, hostility, and corruption rather than a single social relationship. It should be read alongside the chapter’s repeated offers of repentance, which make clear that turning back before death remains a different path.

phrases.translation: Had they believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what has been revealed to him, they would have never taken those ˹pagans˺ as allies.
phrases.explanation: Sincere faith in Allah, His Prophet, and the revelation sent to him would be incompatible with taking pagans as protective allies against the believers. The statement identifies the contradiction between professed belief and hostile allegiance. It concerns loyalty demonstrated through action, not simply claiming belief while supporting those who oppose Allah and His Messenger.

phrases.translation: But most of them are rebellious
phrases.explanation: Rebellion explains why many of them persisted in the contradictory alliance. Their problem was not merely lack of information but departure from obedience to the faith they professed. The verse therefore treats political alignment as spiritually significant when it joins enmity toward Allah, His Prophet, and the believing community.

phrases.translation: You will surely find the most bitter towards the believers to be the Jews and polytheists and the most gracious to be those who call themselves Christian.
phrases.explanation: The verse contrasts groups encountered in the Prophet’s historical setting, describing intense hostility from groups of Jews and polytheists and nearest affection from people calling themselves Christians. The following verses identify particular humble Christians who respond to revelation. This is not permission to hate every Jew or assume every Christian is friendly, but a report that tempers generalizations through actual conduct.

phrases.translation: That is because there are priests and monks among them and because they are not arrogant
phrases.explanation: Priests and monks among these Christians are associated with devotion and knowledge of scripture, while their lack of arrogance makes them receptive to truth. The praised quality is humble religious seriousness rather than a title or monastic status alone. Their learning and worship do not make them defensive when they recognize Allah’s revelation.

phrases.translation: When they listen to what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears for recognizing the truth.
phrases.explanation: When these receptive listeners hear the revelation, their eyes fill with tears because they recognize its truth. Commentators proposed the Negus’s companions or other followers of Jesus who accepted Islam, while al-Tabari left the precise group unnamed. Their emotional response shows humble recognition rather than stubborn argument against what has become clear.

phrases.translation: They say, “Our Lord! We believe, so count us among the witnesses
phrases.explanation: They openly declare faith and ask Allah to register them among the witnesses. This moves beyond tears to commitment and identification with those who testify to the truth. Commentary connects the witnesses with Muhammad’s community, which bears witness before humanity. Their request seeks lasting responsibility and belonging, not only a moving religious experience.

phrases.translation: Why should we not believe in Allah and the truth that has come to us?
phrases.explanation: Their rhetorical question makes faith the reasonable response to Allah and the truth that has reached them. Once truth is recognized, refusing belief would contradict their own conviction. They are not asking for a sign to remove all thought, but expressing why the evidence and their longing for Allah leave no honest reason to turn away.

phrases.translation: And we long for our Lord to include us in the company of the righteous.”
phrases.explanation: Their faith is joined with hope that Allah will admit them among the righteous. They seek the company and outcome of people made upright before Him rather than mere victory in a religious argument. This hope gives their confession a forward direction toward divine acceptance and lasting companionship.

phrases.translation: So Allah will reward them for what they said with Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever.
phrases.explanation: Allah rewards their sincere declaration with gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they remain forever. The reward answers words that expressed genuine recognition, faith, and hope, not empty religious speech. Everlasting gardens far exceed the social or personal cost of accepting truth and joining the witnesses.

phrases.translation: And that is the reward of the good-doers
phrases.explanation: Their outcome is called the reward of those who do good, linking the preceding confession with excellent conduct. Sincere words are accepted because they express a truthful turn toward Allah and a desire for righteous company. The description broadens the lesson beyond this group to the divine principle of rewarding sincere goodness.

phrases.translation: As for those who disbelieve and reject Our signs, they will be the residents of the Hellfire
phrases.explanation: Those who disbelieve and deny Allah’s signs receive the contrasting outcome of Hellfire. The juxtaposition places two responses to revelation side by side: humble recognition leading to gardens and persistent rejection leading to loss. The warning concerns denial of Allah and His signs, not a punishment for failing to display the same emotional response as the tearful listeners.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress.
phrases.explanation: Believers must not declare Allah’s lawful good things forbidden, nor transgress His limits in the opposite direction by permitting what He forbids. Reports describe companions considering extreme renunciation of marriage, food, clothing, or sleep. The verse rejects self-invented severity as well as indulgence, leaving the authority to prohibit and permit with Allah.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors
phrases.explanation: Allah does not love transgressors, whether they exceed His limits through unauthorized prohibition or unauthorized permission. Piety is not measured by how much hardship a person invents. Faithful restraint means remaining within divine guidance, neither treating personal austerity as revelation nor treating desire as a reason to erase divine boundaries.

phrases.translation: Eat of the good, lawful things provided to you by Allah.
phrases.explanation: The believers are expressly told to eat Allah’s lawful and good provision. Enjoying permitted food is not a failure of devotion, and they need not feel guilty for declining self-imposed prohibitions. The command balances the earlier food restrictions with gratitude for abundance, while keeping both lawfulness and wholesomeness as conditions.

phrases.translation: And be mindful of Allah in Whom you believe
phrases.explanation: Mindfulness of Allah, in whom they believe, should accompany eating and other lawful enjoyments. Gratitude and obedience prevent permission from becoming excess or ingratitude. The verse links ordinary nourishment with faith, so a believer honours the Provider both by avoiding what He forbids and by receiving what He allows.

phrases.translation: Allah will not call you to account for your thoughtless oaths, but He will hold you accountable for deliberate oaths.
phrases.explanation: Thoughtless oaths are distinguished from deliberate commitments firmly intended by the heart. Al-Tabari held that the former do not bring accountability, while binding oaths require expiation when broken. Reports also discuss mistaken oaths and oaths to do wrong that should be abandoned for what is better. An oath never makes a sinful act obligatory.

phrases.translation: The penalty for a broken oath is to feed ten poor people from what you normally feed your own family,
phrases.explanation: The first expiation option is feeding ten poor people from the normal middle standard of what one feeds one’s own family, not the poorest scraps or an extravagant display. Jurists discussed precise quantities and meals, while al-Tabari related the standard to a person’s circumstances. This is one alternative, not a requirement to perform every listed option.

phrases.translation: or to clothe them,
phrases.explanation: Clothing the same ten needy people is a separate alternative to feeding them. Al-Tabari held that what genuinely counts as a garment, or more, fulfils this option, while scholars discussed particular sets of clothing. The wording does not make clothing an automatic addition after feeding, but another way to complete the expiation.

phrases.translation: or to free a bondsperson.
phrases.explanation: Freeing a bondsperson is the third material alternative. It makes the granting of someone’s liberty a means of repairing a broken oath within the historical legal setting. Feeding, clothing, and freeing are alternatives from which the expiator may choose according to ability, not three cumulative penalties that everyone must perform together.

phrases.translation: But if none of this is affordable, then you must fast three days.
phrases.explanation: Fasting three days is the fallback for someone unable to afford any of the material alternatives, not an equally open choice for a person who can provide them. Jurists differed over the surplus that counts as ability and whether the days must be consecutive. Al-Tabari allowed consecutive or separated fasting but preferred consecutive days for caution.

phrases.translation: This is the penalty for breaking your oaths.
phrases.explanation: The listed actions constitute the expiation for qualifying broken oaths. Expiation repairs the breach through service, liberation, or fasting when necessary. It is not permission to swear falsely or to purchase indulgence for deliberate deception. The oath’s moral seriousness remains, and an oath to commit wrong should not be fulfilled merely to keep one’s word.

phrases.translation: So be mindful of your oaths.
phrases.explanation: Believers must guard their oaths before and after speaking them. Careless appeals to Allah’s Name should be avoided, deliberate promises should be remembered, and a wrongful promise must not become an excuse for sin. Regular expiation is not the intended way of life. Restraint and honesty are the better protection.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah makes things clear to you, so perhaps you will be grateful
phrases.explanation: Allah explains the distinction between thoughtless and deliberate oaths, the available expiations, and the concession for poverty so that people may act with knowledge and gratitude. Clarity removes both anxious guessing and casual neglect. Gratitude is shown by following the guidance rather than treating the alternatives as technical loopholes.

phrases.translation: O believers! Intoxicants, gambling, idols, and drawing lots for decisions are all evil of Satan’s handiwork.
phrases.explanation: Intoxicants, gambling, idolatrous altars, and divining arrows are called defiling works of Satan. The list joins impaired judgment, unjust gain, false worship, and seeking decisions through fortune. Satan’s handiwork refers to his beautifying and urging these practices, not to removing human responsibility for choosing them. Their shared description marks them as moral and spiritual corruption.

phrases.translation: So shun them so you may be successful
phrases.explanation: The command is to shun these practices so that believers may succeed. Distance is required rather than attempting to make defilement an act of devotion. Success includes freedom from the harm, enmity, and distraction from remembrance and prayer described next. Avoidance protects both worship and relationships within the believing community.

phrases.translation: Satan’s plan is to stir up hostility and hatred between you with intoxicants and gambling and to prevent you from remembering Allah and praying.
phrases.explanation: Satan seeks to use intoxicants and gambling to create hostility and hatred and to obstruct remembrance of Allah and prayer. The prohibition therefore addresses social and spiritual damage, not only personal health or intoxication. Reports proposed several occasions involving drink, gambling, and violence, but no single occasion was certain. Satan’s aim does not remove human responsibility for these choices.

phrases.translation: Will you not then abstain
phrases.explanation: The rhetorical question calls for a definite decision to stop after the harms have been exposed. Knowing that intoxicants and gambling can fracture community and interrupt worship should lead to abstention rather than continued delay. The question appeals to the believers’ own understanding and commitment, inviting them to end conduct whose destructive purpose has now been made clear.

phrases.translation: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware!
phrases.explanation: Obedience to Allah and His Messenger requires acting on the prohibition just announced, while beware adds vigilance against returning to it. The command is not satisfied by acknowledging the harm intellectually. Believers must guard their conduct, resist Satan’s invitation, and remain attentive to the prayer and remembrance that these habits threaten.

phrases.translation: But if you turn away, then know that Our Messenger’s duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly
phrases.explanation: If people turn away after clear delivery, the Messenger has fulfilled his responsibility. His duty is to communicate the message plainly, not to compel obedience or accept blame for every refusal. This does not lessen the seriousness of turning away. It locates responsibility for the response with those who heard and understood the command.

phrases.translation: There is no blame on those who believe and do good for what they had consumed before ˹the prohibition˺, as long as they fear Allah, have faith, and do what is good;
phrases.explanation: There is no blame for what believing, righteous people consumed before the prohibition arrived, provided they continue in mindfulness, faith, and good works. The rule is not applied retroactively to create guilt for an earlier lawful act. It gives no permission to continue after revelation, since the repeated conditions require obedient restraint once Allah’s command is known.

phrases.translation: then they believe and act virtuously, then become fully mindful ˹of Allah˺ and do righteous deeds.
phrases.explanation: The repeated sequence of mindfulness, faith, virtue, and excellent action emphasizes continuing growth and perseverance after new guidance. A person must remain faithful after each obligation rather than relying on an earlier state of belief. Commentary understands the final excellence as going beyond bare duty through voluntary good deeds that draw the servant nearer to Allah.

phrases.translation: For Allah loves the good-doers
phrases.explanation: Allah loves those who do good, which is the goal of the repeated progression just described. Divine love is linked to sustained excellent conduct, not merely to having avoided blame for past consumption. The statement encourages believers to move beyond minimal compliance toward active goodness that reflects gratitude for clear guidance.

phrases.translation: O believers! Allah will surely test you with game within the reach of your hands and spears to distinguish those who fear Him in secret.
phrases.explanation: Allah tests pilgrims by bringing game within reach of their hands and spears while hunting is restricted. The ease of taking it makes restraint a genuine demonstration of private fear of Allah, even without human supervision. The test reveals obedience through experience, not because Allah needs to discover information He does not already know.

phrases.translation: Whoever transgresses from now on will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Transgression after this clear test brings a painful punishment. Once the limit and the deliberate test are known, taking the accessible game becomes a conscious choice to disobey. The warning answers the temptation to assume that an easy opportunity or absence of witnesses makes the violation insignificant.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not kill game while on pilgrimage.
phrases.explanation: Killing game is forbidden while in the consecrated state of Hajj or Umrah. The prohibition belongs to that sacred condition rather than declaring land game permanently unlawful, as the next verse confirms. Pilgrims must therefore restrain ordinary lawful activity when Allah temporarily sets it aside for the discipline and sanctity of pilgrimage.

phrases.translation: Whoever kills game intentionally must compensate by offering its equivalence—as judged by two just men among you—to be offered at the Sacred House,
phrases.explanation: Intentional killing requires compensation through an equivalent from livestock, assessed by two just people and brought as an offering to the Sacred House. Jurists debated whether equivalence meant physical resemblance or monetary valuation, with al-Tabari preferring the closest livestock counterpart. Independent just assessment prevents the offender from casually minimizing the loss.

phrases.translation: or by feeding the needy,
phrases.explanation: Feeding needy people is a second expiation option, with its amount related to the assessed game. Some jurists treated the options as successive fallbacks according to ability, while al-Tabari held that the offender could choose among all three. Feeding is therefore not automatically added to the livestock offering, though its proper measure still requires assessment.

phrases.translation: or by fasting so that they may taste the consequences of their violations.
phrases.explanation: Fasting is another alternative, allowing the offender to experience the consequences of the violation through personal restraint. Its duration corresponds to the assessed feeding obligation rather than automatically copying the three days prescribed for an oath. Jurists differed over the conversion, and al-Tabari preferred one day for each mudd of food in the valuation.

phrases.translation: Allah has forgiven what has been done.
phrases.explanation: Allah announces forgiveness for what has already been done, preventing earlier conduct from becoming a source of continuing retroactive anxiety after the rule is clarified. This backward-looking pardon does not authorize new violations. The following warning expressly separates what was forgiven from the different case of persisting after the command.

phrases.translation: But those who persist will be punished by Allah.
phrases.explanation: Those who persist after the prohibition and its expiations have been made clear will face Allah’s punishment. Repetition demonstrates refusal to accept the sacred limit rather than uncertainty about it. The availability of compensation does not make intentional disobedience harmless or turn pilgrimage restrictions into a fee that can be paid without repentance.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment
phrases.explanation: Allah’s might and ability to punish guarantee that persistent violation cannot escape Him. A pilgrim may be far from observers or able to offer compensation, but neither circumstance places the offender beyond divine authority. The warning closes the ruling with accountability rather than leaving it as a mere ritual technicality.

phrases.translation: It is lawful for you to hunt and eat seafood, as a provision for you and for travellers.
phrases.explanation: Sea hunting and seafood are lawful as provision for residents and travellers, including during pilgrimage. Al-Tabari understood the wording to include freshly caught sea game and what the sea casts ashore, while other interpretations of its food were reported. The permission offers practical nourishment and stands in deliberate contrast with the temporary restriction on land game.

phrases.translation: But hunting on land is forbidden to you while on pilgrimage.
phrases.explanation: Land hunting remains forbidden during the consecrated state, not after pilgrimage ends. Scholars debated the prohibition’s precise scope. Al-Tabari included hunting, killing, buying, and selling, while allowing a pilgrim to eat game lawfully hunted by a non-pilgrim for a non-pilgrim under specified conditions. The core rule is temporary abstention from exploiting land game while consecrated.

phrases.translation: Be mindful of Allah to Whom you all will be gathered
phrases.explanation: Mindfulness of Allah is required because everyone will be gathered back to Him. The permissions and restrictions concerning food are therefore matters of accountability, not trivial travel customs. Remembering the gathering helps pilgrims obey when no one is watching and keeps abundant lawful provision from distracting them from the purpose of worship.

phrases.translation: Allah has made the Ka’bah—the Sacred House—a sanctuary of well-being for all people, along with the sacred months, the sacrificial animals, and the ˹offerings decorated with˺ garlands.
phrases.explanation: The Kaaba, sacred months, offerings, and garlands are made a source of stability and wellbeing for people. Al-Tabari explains that these institutions restrained aggression and supported social order before Islam, while in Islam they also organize pilgrimage and prayer direction. Their sanctity serves human welfare through divinely established limits rather than through human invention.

phrases.translation: All this so you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and that He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of everything
phrases.explanation: These wise institutions should lead people to recognize Allah’s knowledge of everything in heaven and earth. The One who knows what benefits and harms humanity has established their religious order with complete knowledge. Nothing about human behaviour is hidden from Him, so the rules are both meaningful guidance and a reminder of coming accountability.

phrases.translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: Allah is severe in punishment toward persistent disobedience and forgiving and merciful toward those who turn back in repentance. Holding these truths together prevents both careless presumption and despair. The preceding rules should be taken seriously, while past failures should lead to return rather than the belief that mercy is no longer possible.

phrases.translation: The Messenger’s duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺.
phrases.explanation: The Messenger’s duty is to deliver the message, not to force people to obey or to control their hidden response. Once he has conveyed it clearly, reward and punishment belong to Allah. This defines prophetic responsibility without reducing the importance of the message or the listener’s obligation to respond.

phrases.translation: And Allah ˹fully˺ knows what you reveal and what you conceal
phrases.explanation: Allah knows public actions and concealed beliefs, intentions, doubts, and hypocrisy. Outward compliance cannot disguise inward rejection before Him, and private sincerity is not lost when others fail to see it. This comprehensive knowledge makes delivery of the message sufficient, because no listener’s real response ultimately escapes judgment.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Good and evil are not equal, though you may be dazzled by the abundance of evil.
phrases.explanation: Good and evil are not equal even when evil’s abundance is impressive. Numbers, visibility, and material success do not determine moral value or final outcome. Commentary applies the contrast to obedient and disobedient people as well as sound and corrupt things. A majority of wrong cannot turn wrong into good or guarantee success.

phrases.translation: So be mindful of Allah, O people of reason, so you may be successful.”
phrases.explanation: People of reason are told to remain mindful of Allah in order to succeed. Reason should recognize that abundance is not proof of worth, while mindfulness acts on that recognition through obedience. Success comes from choosing good before Allah, not from joining whatever is numerous, fashionable, or outwardly dazzling.

phrases.translation: O believers! Do not ask about any matter which, if made clear to you, may disturb you.
phrases.explanation: The warning concerns excessive or testing questions about matters Allah has left unaddressed and hidden facts whose disclosure could cause harm. Reports include asking who one’s father was, whether Hajj was annual, and questions about pagan animal customs. It is not a ban on beneficial learning, but a caution against demanding answers that may bring painful knowledge or new obligations.

phrases.translation: But if you inquire about what is being revealed in the Quran, it will be made clear to you.
phrases.explanation: When the Quran is being revealed on a matter, inquiry receives clarification. The distinction is therefore not between faith and careful study, but between untimely demands about what has been left open and humble attention to what Allah is actually explaining. Once guidance is given, the believers must accept the answer rather than repeat the question in hopes of a different ruling.

phrases.translation: Allah has forgiven what was done ˹in the past˺.
phrases.explanation: Allah has forgiven what occurred in the past, including the excessive questioning that prompted the rebuke. The believers are not permanently condemned for having asked before receiving this guidance. Forgiveness allows them to change their conduct without despair, while the new instruction governs how they should approach such questions afterward.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation: Allah’s forgiveness and forbearance explain why past questions did not bring immediate punishment. He gives people room to learn, correct themselves, and grow into obedience. Forbearance should not be mistaken for approval of persistent testing or mockery, but it assures those who accept correction that earlier mistakes can be left behind.

phrases.translation: Some people before you asked such questions then denied their answers
phrases.explanation: Earlier peoples asked for signs or rulings and then rejected the answers they received. Commentary mentions those who demanded Salih’s she-camel and people connected with the requested table from heaven. Their failure was not curiosity alone, but refusing to believe after the requested evidence came. The warning asks whether an answer will actually change the questioner’s response.

phrases.translation: Allah has never ordained the ˹so-called˺ baḥîrah, sâ'ibah, waṣîlah, and ḥâm camels.
phrases.explanation: These names refer to pre-Islamic categories of camels marked, released, or exempted from use under customary religious vows. Allah never instituted their claimed sacred status. The verse does not deny that people physically treated animals in these ways. It denies that their human customs were divine commands or valid acts of worship.

phrases.translation: But the disbelievers just fabricate lies about Allah, and most of them lack understanding
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers fabricate lies by attributing their invented permissions and prohibitions to Allah. Al-Tabari distinguished leaders who knowingly instituted corrupt customs from followers who accepted them without understanding. The lack of understanding concerns failure to recognize the false attribution, not a claim about the general intelligence of an entire population.

phrases.translation: When it is said to them, “Come to Allah’s revelations and to the Messenger,” they reply, “What we found our forefathers practicing is good enough for us.”
phrases.explanation: When invited to Allah’s revelation and His Messenger, the custom keepers answer that ancestral practice is sufficient. They make inheritance the final authority even when revelation challenges it. Tradition can preserve valuable knowledge, but here it is used to avoid examining whether a religious rule actually came from Allah.

phrases.translation: ˹Would they still do so,˺ even if their forefathers had absolutely no knowledge or guidance
phrases.explanation: The rhetorical question asks whether ancestral practice remains sufficient even when the ancestors possessed no knowledge or guidance. Lineage and antiquity cannot supply the authority that truth requires. This is not a declaration that every ancestor was misguided, but a refusal to treat ancestry alone as proof that a practice is right.

phrases.translation: O believers! You are accountable only for yourselves.
phrases.explanation: Each believer must care for his or her own soul and answer for personal obedience. The command does not cancel duties toward others, since the surrounding chapter repeatedly requires justice and forbidding evil. It establishes that another person’s deviation cannot serve as an excuse for abandoning one’s own guidance.

phrases.translation: It will not harm you if someone chooses to deviate—as long as you are ˹rightly˺ guided.
phrases.explanation: Another person’s deviation does not harm the believer who remains guided and fulfils the duties owed toward that person. Al-Tabari preferred Abu Bakr’s explanation that this includes enjoining good, forbidding evil, and restraining injustice within one’s ability. After those responsibilities have been fulfilled, persistent refusal by others does not transfer their guilt to the obedient believer.

phrases.translation: To Allah you will all return, and He will inform you of what you used to do
phrases.explanation: Everyone will return to Allah and be informed of their actual deeds. Final judgment is therefore individual and comprehensive rather than based on the success or failure of a surrounding group. This promise gives both warning and reassurance: persistent offenders answer for themselves, and faithful people are not lost because others rejected their sincere efforts.

phrases.translation: O believers! When death approaches any of you, call upon two just Muslim men to witness as you make a bequest;
phrases.explanation: When death approaches and a bequest is made, two just Muslim men are ordinarily called to witness. Their integrity protects the dying person’s instructions and the rights of heirs after the testator can no longer clarify them. Al-Tabari understood from among you as the community of faith rather than restricting the witnesses to the deceased’s tribe.

phrases.translation: otherwise, two non-Muslims if you are afflicted with death while on a journey.
phrases.explanation: The travel setting permits two witnesses from outside the Muslim community when death overtakes people away from their normal community. This is a practical exception for an emergency, not a statement that non-Muslim testimony is inherently deceitful or that trustworthy witnesses may be disregarded. The procedure aims to preserve a bequest where ordinary witnesses are not readily available.

phrases.translation: If you doubt ˹their testimony˺, keep them after prayer and let them testify under oath ˹saying˺, “By Allah!
phrases.explanation: When the witnesses’ handling of an entrusted bequest is doubted or challenged, they are detained after prayer for a solemn oath. Al-Tabari identified the prayer as the afternoon prayer. The public religious setting gives gravity to the testimony and creates a structured way to examine suspicion rather than leaving heirs and witnesses to unresolved accusation.

phrases.translation: We would never sell our testimony for any price, even in favour of a close relative, nor withhold the testimony of Allah.
phrases.explanation: The witnesses swear that they will not exchange testimony for payment, favour even a close relative, or conceal testimony belonging to Allah. The oath excludes both bribery and family bias. Truth is described as a divine trust, so testimony cannot legitimately be treated as personal property to sell, withhold, or redirect toward someone preferred.

phrases.translation: Otherwise, we would surely be sinful.”
phrases.explanation: They acknowledge that violating this oath would make them sinful. The conclusion places moral responsibility directly on the witnesses rather than allowing them to blame pressure, kinship, or an offered price. A false oath compounds betrayal of the deceased and heirs with false speech made in Allah’s Name.

phrases.translation: If they are found guilty ˹of false testimony˺, let the deceased’s two closest heirs affected by the bequest replace the witnesses and testify under oath ˹saying˺, “By Allah!
phrases.explanation: If the original witnesses are subsequently found to have incurred guilt through false testimony or betrayal, two of the deceased’s closest affected heirs take their place and swear. The procedure responds to discovered wrongdoing, not merely to heirs disliking a valid bequest. It gives the injured family a defined way to contest the discredited testimony.

phrases.translation: Our testimony is truer than theirs.
phrases.explanation: The replacement witnesses swear that their testimony has a stronger claim to truth than the discredited witnesses’ testimony. Their standing arises from the exposed falsehood and the procedure, not from a general rule that relatives are always more truthful. The oath formally contests the earlier account after its reliability has collapsed.

phrases.translation: We have not transgressed.
phrases.explanation: They also swear that they have not transgressed. This restrains the heirs as well as the original witnesses, since an injured party can also lie or claim more than is due. Seeking justice for the deceased does not permit false testimony or exceeding the actual right being defended.

phrases.translation: Otherwise, we would surely be wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: The replacement witnesses acknowledge that falsehood would make them wrongdoers. Both sides therefore remain under Allah’s judgment and the moral discipline of the oath. The procedure is not a contest in which family loyalty excuses dishonesty, but a means of reaching truth while warning every participant against injustice.

phrases.translation: In this way it is more likely that witnesses will give true testimony or else fear that their oaths could be refuted by those of the heirs.
phrases.explanation: This procedure makes truthful testimony more likely because witnesses either act faithfully or fear that later oaths will overturn theirs after guilt is exposed. It discourages betrayal without claiming that oaths make error impossible. The arrangement protects the deceased’s wishes and heirs through accountability, solemnity, and the possibility of a subsequent challenge.

phrases.translation: Be mindful of Allah and obey.
phrases.explanation: Mindfulness of Allah and obedient listening are required throughout testimony and inheritance disputes. Participants must hear the warning and act upon it rather than treating the oath as an empty ritual. Reverence guards against false swearing, concealment, and betrayal of property entrusted by someone who can no longer defend his or her wishes.

phrases.translation: For Allah does not guide the rebellious people
phrases.explanation: Allah does not guide people who persist in rebellious departure from His command, including false oaths and betrayal. Al-Tabari regarded this testimony procedure as continuing rather than abrogated. The warning makes honest dealing part of guided conduct, while persistent corruption in legal oaths places a person outside that path.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider˺ the Day Allah will gather the messengers and say, “What response did you receive?”
phrases.explanation: On Judgment Day Allah gathers the messengers and asks what response their communities gave them. The question establishes public accountability for both delivery and reception of revelation. Allah does not need information He lacks. The scene makes the messengers witnesses concerning their mission and makes every community confront its answer to them.

phrases.translation: They will reply, “We have no knowledge ˹compared to You˺! You ˹alone˺ are indeed the Knower of all unseen.”
phrases.explanation: The messengers answer that they have no knowledge compared with Allah, the Knower of all unseen. Al-Tabari explained that they do not deny what they witnessed or later testify about their communities. They disclaim independent or exhaustive knowledge, especially of what happened after them and what hearts concealed, while affirming Allah’s superior knowledge of everything.

phrases.translation: And ˹on Judgment Day˺ Allah will say, “O Jesus, son of Mary! Remember My favour upon you and your mother: how I supported you with the holy spirit so you spoke to people in ˹your˺ infancy and adulthood.
phrases.explanation: Allah reminds Jesus and Mary of His favours, including support through the holy spirit and speech in infancy and adulthood. These extraordinary gifts come from Allah rather than demonstrating independent divinity in Jesus. The address honours him as a recipient of help and revelation before his miracles are recalled in detail.

phrases.translation: How I taught you writing, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel.
phrases.explanation: Allah taught Jesus writing, wisdom, the Torah, and the Gospel. His knowledge and message are therefore learned and received through divine favour, not evidence of an uncreated nature. The list joins practical knowledge and wise judgment with revealed scripture, showing the breadth of his preparation as a messenger.

phrases.translation: How you moulded a bird from clay—by My Will—and breathed into it and it became a ˹real˺ bird—by My Will.
phrases.explanation: Jesus moulded a bird’s form from clay and breathed into it, and it became a real bird by Allah’s permission. The repetition of by My Will on both sides of the miracle prevents it from being read as independent creative power. Jesus performs the appointed actions, while Allah grants the resulting life and reality.

phrases.translation: How you healed the blind and the lepers—by My Will.
phrases.explanation: Jesus healed the blind and lepers by Allah’s will. These genuine healings display divine power and compassion working through His messenger, not a power independent of Allah. The repeated qualification is especially important in a passage addressing exaggerated claims about Jesus, since extraordinary miracles do not make their human instrument divine.

phrases.translation: How you brought the dead to life—by My Will.
phrases.explanation: Bringing the dead to life is again qualified by Allah’s will. Even a miracle that resembles giving life remains an act granted through divine permission rather than evidence that Jesus possesses ultimate life-giving authority himself. The favour belongs to Allah, and the miracle serves as a sign of His power and His messenger’s truth.

phrases.translation: How I prevented the Children of Israel from harming you when you came to them with clear proofs and the disbelievers among them said, “This is nothing but pure magic.”
phrases.explanation: Allah protected Jesus from the Children of Israel when he brought clear proofs, while the disbelievers among them dismissed the miracles as magic. The wording distinguishes those disbelievers from the whole people. Rejection did not make the proofs unclear, and hostile power could not overcome Allah’s protection of His messenger.

phrases.translation: And how I inspired the disciples, “Believe in Me and My messenger!”
phrases.explanation: Allah inspired the disciples, who were Jesus’ helpers in his mission, to believe in Him and in His messenger. Commentary explains the inspiration as revelation or divine inspiration to their hearts. The command distinguishes Allah from Jesus while requiring faith in both the Sender and the truth brought by the messenger.

phrases.translation: They declared, “We believe and bear witness that we fully submit ˹to Allah˺.”
phrases.explanation: The disciples answer with faith and ask Allah to witness their complete submission to Him. Their response is not merely an intellectual acknowledgment of Jesus’ miracles. They commit themselves to obedient surrender before Allah, demonstrating the proper response to the inspiration and to the messenger’s call.

phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when the disciples asked, “O Jesus, son of Mary! Would your Lord be willing to send down to us a table spread with food from heaven?”
phrases.explanation: The disciples ask Jesus whether his Lord will send down a table of food from heaven. Al-Tabari explained the wording as asking whether Allah would answer Jesus’ request, not necessarily doubting divine power. Their request seeks a further sign through the prophet rather than treating Jesus himself as the independent source of the miracle.

phrases.translation: Jesus answered, “Fear Allah if you are ˹truly˺ believers.”
phrases.explanation: Jesus answers by calling them to fear Allah if they are truly believers. The warning teaches that requests for extraordinary signs must not become presumptuous tests of Allah or substitutes for obedience. Faith should govern the manner of asking, and sincere believers must remain mindful of the gravity of demanding direct miraculous assurance.

phrases.translation: They said, “We ˹only˺ wish to eat from it to reassure our hearts, to verify you are indeed truthful to us, and to become its witnesses.”
phrases.explanation: The disciples explain that they want to eat from the table, reassure their hearts, verify Jesus’ truthfulness, and become witnesses to the sign. Their stated aims are nourishment, certainty, and testimony rather than idle spectacle. Even so, the preceding warning remains important: believers should not make obedience conditional on receiving whatever extraordinary proof they request.

phrases.translation: Jesus, son of Mary, prayed, “O Allah, our Lord! Send us from heaven a table spread with food as a feast for us—the first and last of us—and as a sign from You.
phrases.explanation: Jesus prays to Allah as his Lord for the table to be a feast and a sign for present and later followers. Al-Tabari understood the feast as an occasion for worship and gratitude. Commentators disagreed over whether the table actually descended, while al-Tabari held that it did. Jesus’ prayer again shows his dependence on Allah.

phrases.translation: Provide for us! You are indeed the Best Provider.”
phrases.explanation: Jesus asks Allah for provision and calls Him the Best Provider. Even when requesting an extraordinary heavenly meal, he directs the need for sustenance to Allah rather than himself. The title affirms that all provision, ordinary or miraculous, comes from the One best able to give and sustain.

phrases.translation: Allah answered, “I am sending it down to you.
phrases.explanation: Allah answers that He is sending the table down, granting the requested sign through His own action. The promise places the miracle under divine power and generosity rather than human control. Whatever uncertainty later commentators expressed about the historical outcome, the verse itself presents Allah’s answer as a definite commitment to send it.

phrases.translation: But whoever among you denies afterwards will be subjected to a torment I have never inflicted on anyone of My creation.”
phrases.explanation: Disbelief after receiving the requested sign brings an exceptionally severe punishment because it follows specially granted clarity. Al-Tabari understood anyone of creation in this context as the people of that time. The warning shows that demanding further evidence increases responsibility. A miraculous answer must lead to faithfulness, not to renewed rejection after the request has been fulfilled.

phrases.translation: And ˹on Judgment Day˺ Allah will say, “O Jesus, son of Mary! Did you ever ask the people to worship you and your mother as gods besides Allah?”
phrases.explanation: Allah asks Jesus whether he ever told people to worship him and Mary as gods besides Allah. Commentary reports both a Judgment Day setting and a setting when Jesus was raised, with al-Tabari preferring the latter. The question gives Jesus the opportunity to testify to his actual teaching, not an attempt by Allah to obtain unknown information.

phrases.translation: He will answer, “Glory be to You! How could I ever say what I had no right to say?
phrases.explanation: Jesus glorifies Allah and denies that he could say something for which he had no right. His first response is reverence for divine uniqueness, followed by rejection of the attributed teaching. He does not accept honour that belongs only to Allah or defend himself by minimizing the seriousness of such a claim.

phrases.translation: If I had said such a thing, you would have certainly known it.
phrases.explanation: Jesus adds that if he had made the statement, Allah would certainly have known it. His denial rests on Allah’s complete knowledge of speech and action. This also clarifies the purpose of the question: public vindication of the messenger and exposure of the false attribution, rather than uncertainty on Allah’s part.

phrases.translation: You know what is ˹hidden˺ within me, but I do not know what is within You.
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what is within Jesus, while Jesus knows only what Allah has disclosed to him. The contrast affirms that even the messenger’s inner reality is fully known to Allah, whereas divine unseen knowledge is not at Jesus’ disposal. Prophetic knowledge remains granted knowledge, not omniscience.

phrases.translation: Indeed, You ˹alone˺ are the Knower of all unseen
phrases.explanation: Jesus concludes that Allah alone is the Knower of all unseen. This final declaration places hidden thoughts, unrecorded speech, and divine realities under Allah’s knowledge alone. It completes his disavowal of deification by distinguishing the limited servant who speaks from the all-knowing Lord who judges.

phrases.translation: I never told them anything except what You ordered me to say: “Worship Allah—my Lord and your Lord!”
phrases.explanation: Jesus summarizes his entire teaching as the message Allah commanded: worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. He taught the same servitude for himself and his people rather than inviting them to worship him. This positive statement accompanies his denial, establishing what he actually preached instead of the doctrine later attributed to him.
